title: Muscle-coordination networks on GRABMyo reproduce across data halves

dataset.name: GRABMyo
dataset.citation: Pradhan A, He J, Jiang N. Multi-day dataset of forearm and wrist electromyogram for hand gesture recognition and biometrics. Sci Data. 2022;9:733.

proposition: On real GRABMyo forearm EMG, the ecosystem's inter-muscle coordination network is reproducible across independent data halves: coherence connectivity replicates near-perfectly (edge r = 0.994, node-strength r = 0.997), with weighted phase-lag index (edge r = 0.835) and directed Granger causality (edge r = 0.939) also reproducible.

claims.statement: split-half edge-weight correlation, directed Granger causality

validation.reference: split-half reproducibility (edge-weight and node-strength correlation) on the real signal
validation.data: REAL — GRABMyo v1.1.0 forearm EMG (10-node coordination network)
validation.note: Coherence, wPLI and directed-GC networks reproduce across halves (edge r 0.835-0.994). Node-strength topology is highly reproducible for coherence (0.997) and wPLI (0.929); partial-coherence node strength is lower (0.572), consistent with the sparser partial-coherence graph being more sensitive to the split.

open_questions.q: Partial-coherence node-strength reproducibility (0.572) is lower than its edge-weight reproducibility (0.975) because the partial-coherence graph is sparse; documented as a known method-sensitivity, not escalated.
